note: The static-analysis tools of T26, and what identifies each: a version and the sha256 of files inside it. Paths are relative to the tools folder ($IWA_TOOLS, else $HOME/tools). `check_tools.py` compares an install with this file. A tool the owner installed from an official archive is identified by its files; the archive's published checksum is recorded where the source publishes one.

tools.name: ghidra

archive.name: ghidra_12.1.4_PUBLIC_20260921.zip
archive.published_by: the release page of the source

tools.runs: support/analyzeHeadless <project folder> <project name> -import <file> -processor "x86:LE:16:Real Mode" -cspec default -scriptPath tools/static/ghidra -postScript T26Report.java <report file> [<needle>...] -log <log file>; needs JAVA_HOME at JDK 21 or later (tools/static/ghidra_import.py sets it)

tools.name: java

archive.name: the Temurin 21.0.12.1+1 Linux x64 JDK tarball

tools.runs: bin/java; Ghidra 12 needs a JDK 21 or later, found through JAVA_HOME

tools.name: projectorrays

build_dependencies.name: libboost1.83-dev
build_dependencies.use: headers only, unpacked below the tools folder

build_dependencies.name: libmpg123-dev
build_dependencies.use: the header, unpacked below the tools folder; the library is the system libmpg123.so.0

tools.runs: bin/projectorrays decompile <movie> -o <existing folder> --dump-scripts | --dump-json [-v]; reads a movie by its own offsets, so tools/static/iwp_extract.py gives it a work copy of the projector's movie at its original offset

tools.name: deark
tools.source: https://github.com/jsummers/deark (tag v1.7.3, commit e3c0ef3c6b6b8b697146a4016eb796ac02744785, an MIT-style licence)
tools.built_by: make in the source tree, without changes (the main session, 2026-10-05, the owner's choice)
tools.runs: deark -m pklite -d -od <run folder> -o stage1-pklite <ISLEWAR.EXE>, then deark -m exepack -d -od <run folder> -o stage2-exepack <the first output>; tools/static/dos_unpack.py runs both

terminal_only.name: objdump
terminal_only.path_class: a system package's binary found on PATH (objdump is the distribution's link to its x86-64 binutils binary), not below the tools folder
terminal_only.source: Ubuntu package binutils-x86-64-linux-gnu 2.42-4ubuntu2.8 (source package binutils), installed with the system; the binary's md5 equals the package's own md5sums entry
terminal_only.use: T26 only: while locating the places that push ISLEWAR.SAV's descriptor, the implementer looked at bytes of the unpacked DOS image with objdump -m i8086, in the terminal. Nothing it printed was kept or tracked, and no script runs it; the probe's addresses and reading are Ghidra's. check_tools.py does not check it.
